judgment.quote_A: The space complexity is O(n) as well, because the maximum size of the stack is equal to the length of the longest unbalanced sequence of parentheses
judgment.quote_B: The extra space complexity is O(n/2) or O(n), since the stack can grow to half the size of the input string in the worst-case scenario (if the input string consists of only alternating opening and closing parentheses)
judgment.reason: Both answers provide the correct stack-based function that ignores non-parenthesis characters, but both omit the explicitly requested tests for 'a(b)c', ')(', and '(()', and both are truncated mid-sentence (finish: length). Answer A correctly identifies the O(n) space complexity worst case as an input of all opening parentheses, while Answer B incorrectly claims the worst case is 'alternating opening and closing parentheses' (which would actually result in O(1) stack space). Thus A is more correct despite both being incomplete.
